Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure happens when constructing a Fraction from a double value close to a simple fraction with maxDenominator constraint. The test creates a Fraction from the value 0.5000000001 with a max denominator of 10 but an overflow exception occurs, which is unexpected.

Inspecting the Fraction constructor with signature Fraction(double, int) shows it delegates to Fraction(double, double, int, int) with epsilon=0 and maxIterations=100.

The main conversion logic in the Fraction(double, double, int, int) constructor uses a continued fraction algorithm to approximate the double value. Variables p2 and q2 represent numerator and denominator candidates respectively, updated each iteration. There is a critical check for overflow in line 212-215: if either numerator or denominator candidate exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE, a FractionConversionException is thrown.

The issue arises because when the value is very close to a simple fraction (e.g., 1/2), the next iteration of the continued fraction computation causes q2 (denominator candidate) or p2 (numerator candidate) to exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE, triggering the exception. But since the value is close to a simple fraction and maxDenominator constraint is small (10), ideally the constructor should return the simple fraction without overflow.

The comment in lines 213-214 indicates awareness of this case: "if the last fraction was very close to the actual value, q2 may overflow in the next iteration; in this case return the last one." Currently, the code throws an exception instead of returning the last convergent fraction before overflow.

Thus, the root cause is that the overflow check throws an exception immediately without considering if the previous convergent fraction (p1/q1) sufficiently approximates the value within the constraints. This leads to failure when the input double is very close to a simple fraction and the next iteration would cause overflow, instead of returning the last valid fraction. The test case exposes this by using 0.5000000001 which is close to 1/2 but causes overflow in next iteration denominator.

Recent bug reports are unrelated, indicating this is a standalone issue with fraction construction overflow handling.

Fixing this requires modifying the overflow handling logic in Fraction(double, double, int, int) to catch this edge case and return the last valid fraction rather than throwing an exception when overflow occurs in next iteration after approximation is sufficiently close.

This diagnosis directly explains the test failure and matches the current bug report describing an overflow when constructing fractions close to a simple fraction with maxDenominator.

Recommended location to fix is in constructor Fraction(double, double, int, int).
org.apache.commons.math3.fraction.Fraction.Fraction(double,double,int,int)
